files.why: No locale mechanism exists yet; add a domain-free reactive source of the user's active language (Locale type + useLocale) — belongs in shared/lib alongside the other framework-light composable useDebounce, and contains no domain nouns.
Composition-root concern: detect/select the user's language (browser default -> de) once at startup, mirroring the existing msw.ts / errorBoundary.ts provider pattern.
Wire the locale provider into bootstrap so the active language is set before the app mounts.

Per-slice presentation mapping of InvoiceStatus (+overdue) to a localized label; a translation table changes for copy/localization reasons, not business-rule reasons, so it is UI, not core, and stays inside billing because it names a domain noun.
Per-slice presentation mapping of AppointmentStatus to a localized label, same rationale as billing's — lives in scheduling/ui, cannot go in shared/ (domain noun).
Only place invoice status text is rendered; replace the raw props.status / "overdue" string with the localized label from useInvoiceStatusLabel.
Only place appointment status text is rendered; replace the inline {{ status }} (and the hardcoded "Conflict") with the localized label from useAppointmentStatusLabel.

uncertain: core/ vs ui/ for the label tables: I placed them in ui/composables because translations change for localization reasons (not business-rule reasons per constitution rule 6) and the existing status->badge-variant maps already live in the UI components. A reasonable teammate could argue the status label is a property of the domain and belongs in core/; I chose ui/ but flag it.

ClientOverviewView.vue (app view) hardcodes an "overdue" badge and appointment cards there show no status — if "statuses" includes that overdue badge, this file (and possibly a new label export on billing/index.ts) would also change. Left out of the definite list pending scope confirmation.

Whether the locale primitive should be shared/lib (framework-light composable, like useDebounce) or shared/ui. I chose shared/lib; if it must stay vue-free it may need to be split into a plain state module plus a ui composable.

Adding tests: the repo has core/mapper tests but no UI/composable tests, so I did not assume a test file. If label coverage is wanted, new tests (e.g. tests/billing.labels.test.ts) would be added following existing Vitest conventions.
questions: Where do the German status strings come from — do you want them inlined in the per-slice label tables now, or is a real i18n library (e.g. vue-i18n) / translation-file workflow expected? That changes the shared primitive substantially.

How is the user's language determined: browser Accept-Language / navigator.language, a user preference persisted server-side, a URL/route locale, or a manual switcher? This decides what the app/providers/locale wiring reads.
Is scope strictly the two status labels, or does "display in the user's language" also cover dates and currency (format.ts is hardcoded to en-US) and the derived "overdue"/"Conflict" badges?
Which locales must launch (just en + de, or a broader set) and what is the fallback when a status has no translation for the active locale?
Do the German status strings need design/legal sign-off (e.g. invoice "void" -> "storniert"/"ungueltig"), and is there a glossary I should follow?
